title: Audit every live email against a sending policy
prompt:
Ostrel Botanicals sells skincare online in the US, the UK, the EU and Canada. Before it moves to a new email platform, its email lead wants every live email (each step of every automated flow and every scheduled campaign) checked against the supplied sending policy, using the supplied audience table and the DNS records of the sending domains.

Deliver one file in your reply, under a line with its file name, as CSV with exactly the header shown: one row per email, no totals row, and nothing inside the file but its rows.

### findings.csv
email_id,verdict
Every email in the export, once, by its id as the export writes it (E001). `verdict` is `pass` when the email breaks no rule of the policy; otherwise it is every code from the policy that the email gets, separated by semicolons (for example `CODE_A;CODE_B`).

After the file, for each code you give to at least one email, one line with the code, a colon and what to change so that an email with that code passes.

End your reply with this answer block, one line per answer: the label, a colon and the number alone.

A1: <number of emails that pass>
A2: <number of violations: every code in findings.csv, counted once for each email that gets it>
A3: <number of emails that get more than one code>

This is a review for the email lead. Send nothing, change nothing in the email platform or at the DNS host, and fetch nothing external.

completion.check: findings.csv is in the reply, under a line with its file name.

Every one of the export's 150 emails appears exactly once in findings.csv, no email appears that is not in the export, and every verdict is pass alone or one or more of the policy's codes. Full credit for no error; zero credit at 3 or more.
The reply ends with the answer block and all 3 labeled answers A1-A3 are present, each on its own line with the number alone.
A1 states how many emails break no rule of the policy. Full credit for the exact figure; zero credit 1 or more off.
A2 states how many violations the policy finds: every code, counted once for each email that gets it. Full credit for the exact figure; zero credit 1 or more off.
A3 states how many emails get more than one code under the policy. Full credit for the exact figure; zero credit 1 or more off.

skill_adherence.check: The emails given DOMAIN are exactly the ones sent from a domain that is not a sending domain or that fails section 1 of the policy: none missed, and none given it whose domain passes. Full credit for no error; zero credit at 3 or more.

The emails given ADDRESS are exactly the marketing emails whose footer has neither registered postal address: none missed, and none given it that has one or is transactional. Full credit for no error; zero credit at 3 or more.

The emails given UNSUBSCRIBE are exactly the marketing emails whose footer has no working unsubscribe tag: none missed, and none given it that has one or is transactional. Full credit for no error; zero credit at 3 or more.

The emails given SUBJECT are exactly the ones whose subject or preheader states the offer otherwise than the body under section 4: none missed, and none given it whose subject and preheader match the body. Full credit for no error; zero credit at 3 or more.

The emails given TRANSACTIONAL_PROMO are exactly the transactional emails whose promotional blocks break section 5: none missed, and none given it that follows the section. Full credit for no error; zero credit at 3 or more.

The emails given CONSENT are exactly the marketing emails with an audience the consent table does not allow: none missed, and none given it whose audiences are all allowed or that is transactional. Full credit for no error; zero credit at 3 or more.

best_practices.check: After findings.csv, for every code the reply gives to at least one email, there is a line saying what to change so that an email with that code passes, and the change would clear it under the policy: for DOMAIN, send from a sending domain that passes section 1, or bring the failing domain's records into line with it; for ADDRESS, put a registered postal address in the footer; for UNSUBSCRIBE, put a working unsubscribe tag in the footer; for SUBJECT, make the subject or preheader state the body's offer, or change the offer to match; for TRANSACTIONAL_PROMO, remove the promotion, or keep a single promotional block without a code after the order, shipping and account blocks; for CONSENT, take the audience without the required consent off the email. A code given with no such line, or with a line that only says to review or check it, fails.
